scopeOfAccept: Accepts sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v1 as a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED leftover-design fixture-authoring artifact under D-056 Decision 5 and D-293 Decision 8, binding nothing. This is not a SATISFIED-GRADE cycle. The accept covers that both authored fixtures conform to the closed d9-exit-contract.v1.14 vocabulary and HostTermination union they claim to draw from, that the subject's custody, quotation and negative claims are measured true against live bytes, and that leftover-design of OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX correctly remains open. It does not SATISFY DR-122, does not close leftover-design, does not execute anything, does not remasure leftover-join.v4, and does not authorize a recording.
rationale: Fourteen prompt attacks and nine further attacks of my own were run against live bytes; all twenty-three were refuted. The freeze conditions hold exactly at both ends of the review: subject ae642e9e... and both fixtures unmoved at mode 0444, with HEAD, COORD, file 08 and the DR-122 status token all matching the prompt and the subject's own pins. All twenty recordedInputs digests recompute with zero mismatches, every basedOn pair agrees with recordedInputs, and the subject satisfies its own remeasurementClause. The substantive claims were verified by construction rather than inspection: I parsed both fixtures and checked each field against the live closed union — REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION is an existing errorCodes member, interrupted requires exactly signal, SIGTERM is in the live signal enum, runId is omitted rather than null as nullabilityPolicy demands, and neither payload carries an unknown member or exitCode. Every string labelled verbatim was tested by literal containment and all five located exactly, including the four nonAuthority rules, which I attacked first as a suspected paraphrase and found to be byte-exact. The sharpest available attack is class collapse, and the record itself spends four clauses drawing the FC-NONAUTH-TERM / FC-OUTFAIL line: the subject not only stays on the right side of it but declines the one in-vocabulary code that would have straddled it, naming OUTPUT.SERIALIZATION_FAILED explicitly as not used. The second sharpest is over-claiming closure, and leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded is empty while OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX survives in five separate places, which is the correct D-294 posture. The OQ-SARIF identifiers looked like minting on first inspection, with numbering gapped at 1, 3, 6, 7 and 8; tracing them to the live D1 register refuted that and showed the gaps are other classes' questions and the recorded standings faithful to the register's own dispositions. Wording is clean of the defects this lineage has been rejected for before: no deictic self-reference, no bare version token in an ambiguous position, no unchanged or byte-identical claim about prose. Five observations are recorded, the strongest being that case 1's missing class discriminator could let a host refuse on schema grounds rather than authority grounds; it is not charged because the shape is declared rather than hidden, adding the discriminator would blur the two cases the record keeps separate, and execution is explicitly qualification. Zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX survive verification.
verdictStatement: ACCEPT — 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. The subject and both fixtures retained their required SHA-256 values and mode 0444 at the start and end of the review. Both authored payloads are witness-byte selections inside the closed d9-exit-contract.v1.14 vocabulary and HostTermination union: an existing errorCodes member with no class discriminator, and the recorded interrupted variant with signal SIGTERM and runId omitted per nullabilityPolicy. The two namedCases stay separate, FC-OUTFAIL stays unauthored and OUTPUT.SERIALIZATION_FAILED stays unused, Coverage preservation stays excluded, SARIF stays unadvertised and G17 unresurrected. The D-002 platform list is quoted byte-exact from G10 occupancy v2 and reproduces ORDERED-EQUAL against G23 occupancy v2, with no per-platform copies on disk. HEAD b993902 is live, D-295 is the last heading, required-now remains 28, file 08 and COORD are unmoved, the DR-122 token remains PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, and leftover-join.v4 remains the current DR-122 leftover-join. The artifact neither SATISFIES DR-122, closes leftover-design of OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX, remasures leftover-join.v4, mints a D9 code or exit number, invents an identifier or a section 7.1 recipe, opens Class A, executes anything, nor authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
